findings_addressed: FIX-2 [P1] — THE TIER-RULE DEFAULT RESOLVED AGAINST THE INSTALLED PACKAGE, NOT THE SURVEYED REPOSITORY. `survey.run_survey` defaulted to `load_tier_map(DEFAULT_TIERS_FILE)` and `paths.DEFAULT_TIERS_FILE` was `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / 'tiers.toml'` — the source tree when run from a checkout, but `site-packages/sbom_survey/` after a NON-EDITABLE install, where the file does not exist because `pyproject.toml` declares no package data (confirmed by listing site-packages). REPRODUCED BEFORE THE FIX: `pip install ./scripts/sbom-survey` -> install_rc=0, then `sbom-survey --repo . --offline --out DIR` -> `sbom-survey: unexpected internal error: FileNotFoundError(2, 'No such file or directory')`, CLI_RC=1. That is EXACTLY the TC-111 install-then-run flow Slice 33 is required to use, so the leg-3 hand-off died on its first command unless the caller happened to pass `--tiers`.

FIX-2 — ROUTE TAKEN: DERIVE FROM `repo_root`, NOT PACKAGE THE FILE AS PACKAGE DATA. codex named both routes and the orchestrator declined to choose; this is the defence. (1) THE RULES ARE DATA ABOUT A REPOSITORY, NOT ABOUT THIS TOOL — every rule is a path prefix into the surveyed tree (`src/rust/crates/`, `dev/tools/`, `Cargo.`), so a copy baked into a wheel describes whichever repository the wheel was built from: meaningless, and silently wrong, when surveying a different one. (2) PACKAGING IT WOULD STOP THE ORACLE GRADING THE FILE THE TOOL USES — `AC-SBOM-08` and `AC-SBOM-11` load the TRACKED `tiers.toml` and compare it against the document `run_survey()` produced with no `tier_map`; with a wheel-bundled default those two could diverge and the criteria would be grading a file the survey never read, which is the TC-105 boundary class this slice has fought from the start. Resolved from `repo_root` they are byte-for-byte the same file, because `conftest.PROJECT_ROOT / 'tiers.toml'` IS `<REPO_ROOT>/scripts/sbom-survey/tiers.toml`. (3) A PACKAGED COPY CAN GO STALE — editing the tracked rules without reinstalling would silently re-tier every component, the event REQ-4 exists to make loud. Consequence: `pyproject.toml` was NOT touched; no `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` entry was needed.

FIX-2 — THE COST OF THAT ROUTE, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Surveying a repository that does not track `scripts/sbom-survey/tiers.toml` now REQUIRES an explicit `--tiers`. That is correct rather than unfortunate: §5.3 rules that there is deliberately NO catch-all rule, so inventing a default rule set for an unknown repository would be precisely the silent mis-tag REQ-4 forbids. It is recorded in the README's new 'Running the tool' section so Slice 33 meets it in documentation rather than at a prompt.

FIX-2 — LOUD, LEGIBLE FAILURE ON THE ERROR PATH, which the orchestrator called for independently of the route. A tool whose entire purpose is failing loudly on an unclassified manifest must not itself die with an unhandled stdlib exception. New `TierRuleFileNotFoundError(TierRuleFileError)`, raised by `load_tier_map`, naming the file it wanted, WHERE THAT PATH COMES FROM, and the `--tiers` override; `load_tier_map` also now converts a `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError` into a `TierRuleFileError` instead of letting it escape. The CLI catches `TierRuleFileError` around `run_survey` and returns 3 — consistent with how it already treats an unreadable explicit `--tiers` — instead of falling through to the bare `Exception` handler and exit 1. VERIFIED against a scratch git repo with no tracked rules: exit 3, the full message, no traceback. AND THE ADVICE IN THE MESSAGE WAS VERIFIED TO WORK: `--tiers FILE` on that same repo exits 0, so the remedy is real rather than plausible.

FIX-2 — ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE, each rc captured on the line immediately after its command. install_rc=0 then CLI_RC=0 for `pip install ./scripts/sbom-survey` + `sbom-survey --repo . --offline --out DIR`, writing all three artifacts over 774 components. MISSING_RC=3 for the same installed binary against a repository with no tracked rules. REMEDY_RC=0 for the documented `--tiers` override. SRC_RC=0 for the source-tree path (`PYTHONPATH=scripts/sbom-survey python -m sbom_survey …`). DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 1/3 — THE TIER OF A COMPONENT REACHABLE FROM SEVERAL MANIFESTS. §5.3 fixes the tier of a MANIFEST; it does not say what tier a COMPONENT takes when it is declared by more than one manifest, or when it is a transitive with no declaring manifest at all. RESOLUTION, forced by the frozen oracle: a component's tier candidates are the tiers of its DECLARING MANIFESTS when it has any, and otherwise the tiers of the LOCKFILES that resolved it; the highest-priority tier wins (shipped > dev-tooling > eval-only, i.e. TIER_VOCABULARY order). With exactly one origin this reduces to that origin's tier, which is what AC-SBOM-11 requires. NOTE the consequence, stated rather than hidden: `packaging` is both a transitive of the shipped src/python/uv.lock AND a direct dependency of this dev-tooling mini-project, so it tiers dev-tooling. Including the lockfile tier in the candidate set would make it `shipped` and would then FAIL AC-SBOM-11, since it carries exactly one origin. Origins-win is therefore the rule the frozen oracle demands, not a preference.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY 2/3 — WHICH VERSIONS A MANIFEST DECLARATION ATTACHES TO. **SUPERSEDED AT FIX-1; THE ROUND-0 RESOLUTION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPLACED.** §5.5 defines direct-ness by NAME ('the package name appears in a dependency table'), while components are identified per (ecosystem, name, version). At round 0 I resolved that as 'attach the declaration to every component sharing its (ecosystem, name)' and flagged it as a deliberate choice. It is not defensible: where a lockfile carries several versions of one name, it stamps a constraint on versions that constraint cannot resolve to, and it marks them `direct`. codex §9 round 1 caught it and it is the round's single [P2]. THE CORRECTED RESOLUTION: a declaration attaches only to the locked entries its constraint ADMITS, evaluated with the ecosystem's own comparator; a name with exactly one candidate is attached unconditionally (no ambiguity to resolve); and a constraint that admits none — or cannot be evaluated — attaches to none of them and records why on an unresolved component, never widening. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED from the round-0 entry: pypi names are canonicalized per PEP 503, so a `pyproject.toml` saying `PyYAML` and a lock saying `pyyaml` are one package; and a declared name with NO lock entry anywhere still materializes an UNRESOLVED component (version omitted, purl without an @version segment, `fathomdb:resolution='unresolved'`). That last case is real here — maturin, networkx, numpy, pyyaml, scipy, plus this tool's own cyclonedx-python-lib / packageurl-python / semver — and is exactly the shape test_cyclonedx.py and test_report.py were written to accommodate, which is why `fathomdb:resolution == 'unresolved'` is required by the tests while §5 never spells it out.
